system.name: xUI
system.one_liner: processor extensions that build on Intel UIPI to deliver low-latency, flexible interrupt-based notification without polling

components.name: Processor Core (Sender)
components.role: sender-side core executing SENDUIPI to post an interrupt

components.name: Local Apic (Sender)
components.role: sender's local APIC that writes ICR to dispatch the interrupt over the system bus

components.name: Interrupt Command Register (ICR)
components.role: register written with receiver APICID/vector to trigger sending

components.name: Mem
components.role: shared memory holding the UPID that coordinates sender and receiver

components.name: UPID
components.role: user posted-interrupt descriptor updated by the sender and read by the receiver's microcode

components.name: Processor Core (Receiver)
components.role: receiver-side core that runs microcode to process and deliver the interrupt

components.name: Micro Seq ROM (MSROM)
components.role: microcode ROM implementing UI notification-processing and delivery procedures

components.name: Program Code (Receiver)
components.role: receiver's user-level interrupt handler, exited via uiret

components.name: UIRR
components.role: register holding the delivered user interrupt vector

components.name: UIF
components.role: user interrupt flag gating interrupt delivery

components.name: Local Apic (Receiver)
components.role: receiver's local APIC that raises the interrupt signal line to the core

components.name: End of Interrupt Register (EOI)
components.role: register signaling interrupt completion to the receiver's local APIC

flows.what: looks up receiver's UPID in the UITT, updates PIR, sets the outstanding-interrupt (ON) bit
sending core reads APICID/vector from UPID and writes ICR
IOAPIC sends the interrupt over the system bus; local APIC raises the interrupt signal line
full pipeline flush; MSROM notification processing reads the vector from UPID into UIRR, clears outstanding bit
delivery microcode pushes stack pointer/PC/vector, clears UIF, jumps to UINT_Handler
uiret pops stack pointer and PC, sets UIF, resumes normal control flow

content.key_idea: Figure 1 traces the seven microcode-driven steps Intel UIPI uses to post and deliver a user interrupt purely through shared memory (UPID) and APIC registers, without kernel involvement or polling.

evidence: Figure 1 illustrates the end-to-end process of sending and receiving a posted UIPI
The sender communicates the UIPI vector through shared memory (UPID)
UIPI is largely implemented in microcode

summary: This paper studies Extended User Interrupts (xUI), processor extensions built on Intel's existing UIPI mechanism for low-latency, poll-free notification. Before introducing xUI's own extensions, the paper analyzes UIPI itself, and this figure gives that architecture view: a Sender and a Receiver processor core, each with Program Code and a Local Apic, communicate through a shared-memory UPID and the system bus. Seven numbered steps trace a posted interrupt end-to-end: the sender updates the UPID and its outstanding-interrupt bit, writes the Interrupt Command Register, and the local APIC signals the receiver over the bus; the receiver's Micro Seq ROM (MSROM) microcode then flushes the pipeline, reads the vector into UIRR, delivers it by jumping to the user handler, and the handler eventually executes uiret to restore the flag UIF and resume execution. Pale color blocks distinguish the memory, code, and microcode regions.
summary_zh: 该图展示Intel UIPI架构：发送核更新共享内存UPID并写入ICR，经系统总线通知接收核；接收核微码MSROM刷新流水线、读取向量至UIRR并跳转用户处理程序，最终uiret恢复UIF。xUI在此基础上扩展。
notes: All components are marked non-novel: the figure documents the pre-existing Intel UIPI mechanism that xUI (introduced later in the paper) extends, not xUI's own new mechanisms.
